Recruitment Fraud Alert

We’ve learned that scammers are impersonating Commvault team members—including HR and leadership—via email or text. These bad actors may conduct fake interviews and ask for personal information, such as your social security number.  

What to know:

  • Commvault does not conduct interviews by email or text.
  • We will never ask you to submit sensitive documents (including banking information, SSN, etc) before your first day.
  • Commvault recruiters may contact prospective candidates through LinkedIn and other professional networking platforms regarding career opportunities. If you are unsure whether a recruiting communication is legitimate, review the profile to ensure they have a badge verifying them as a Commvault employee.

If you suspect a recruiting scam, please contact us at wwrecruitingteam@commvault.com

Engineer – Development, Indexing (C++ / SQL)

Experience: 0–2 years; Fresh graduates are welcome
Location: Bangalore

 The Opportunity

We are looking for an Engineer to join our Indexing team. You will contribute to software that organizes and retrieves data efficiently, with a focus on correctness, performance, and reliability. You will also develop automation to improve testing, validation, and engineering workflows.

This role is suited to an early-career developer with strong C++ and SQL skills, a systematic approach to development, and the curiosity to ask what could go wrong and how to test it.

What you’ll do

  • Develop and maintain indexing components using C++ and SQL.
  • Build and maintain automated tests, validation scripts, and tools that reduce repetitive work.
  • Investigate defects by reproducing issues, examining logs, stepping through code, and identifying root causes.
  • Write SQL queries to retrieve, validate, and troubleshoot data.
  • Design test cases covering expected behaviour, boundary conditions, invalid inputs, and failure scenarios.
  • Add unit and regression tests to validate changes and prevent recurring defects.
  • Work with developers and QA engineers to clarify requirements, review changes, and resolve issues.
  • Communicate findings, explain technical decisions, and document your work clearly.

Who you are

  • A fresh graduate or developer with up to two years of software development experience. Relevant academic projects and internships are welcome.
  • Proficient in C++, including object-oriented programming, STL containers, pointers, references, and memory management.
  • Comfortable writing SQL queries using joins, aggregations, and subqueries, with an understanding of relational database fundamentals.
  • Strong in data structures, algorithms, and logical problem-solving.
  • Able to debug methodically, test assumptions, and explain how you arrived at a solution.
  • Able to translate a requirement into varied test scenarios, including empty or duplicate data, boundary values, large inputs, and interrupted operations.
  • Interested in automation and identifying opportunities to improve testing and development efficiency.
  • Clear in written and verbal communication, willing to ask questions, and receptive to feedback.
  • Curious about unfamiliar code and motivated to learn.

Good to have

  • Familiarity with Python for scripting, automation, or testing.
  • Exposure to test automation frameworks.
  • Understanding of indexing, search, database internals, or storage systems.
  • Familiarity with multithreading, concurrency, and operating system fundamentals.
  • Experience using Git and a debugger such as GDB or Visual Studio.
  • Projects or internships demonstrating C++, SQL, debugging, automation, or thoughtful testing.

About the role We're hiring two backend-heavy full-stack engineers (SDE 2 or SDE 3) for the Cowork team at Sarvam. Cowork is the agentic side of Indus: users hand it real work, and an agent plans, uses tools and connectors, works in a cloud sandbox, and hands back files, docs and artifacts across web, Android, iOS, macOS and Windows. The role is full stack, but the centre of gravity is the backend: the BFF that every client talks to, and increasingly the agent harness behind it. You'll ship features end to end, from the API and data model through to the client screens on mobile, desktop and web. What you'll work on Most of your time goes into the BFF and the services around it; the rest into client work and the harness, depending on what the roadmap needs that quarter. BFF (Chat Service): design and own the APIs that web, mobile and desktop share: sessions, conversations, streaming turns, artifacts, connectors, custom and managed agents. Data modelling, migrations, auth and RBAC, pagination and search. Real-time streaming: stream LLM output, tool calls and agent events from the harness to clients over an event bus, and keep it correct under reconnects, retries and partial failures. Agent harness and platform: contribute to Panja, our agent harness: tool and MCP integrations, sandboxed execution, file and artifact flows, latency and token-cost work. Clients: build features end to end on our Kotlin/Compose Multiplatform apps (Android, iOS, macOS, Windows) and the Next.js web app, so a feature you design in the backend reaches users on every surface. Production ownership: observability, on-call, RCAs, and making the system faster and cheaper with numbers to back it. Tech stack Python and PostgreSQL are the core; you don't need every item below on day one. Backend: Python, SQLAlchemy + Alembic, PostgreSQL, OpenAPI Supporting services: Go Mobile and desktop: Kotlin Multiplatform + Compose Multiplatform (Android, iOS, macOS, Windows) Web: Next.js, React, TypeScript What we're looking for A strong backend engineer who has also shipped real frontend work and is happy to keep doing both. 3+ years (SDE 2) or 5+ years (SDE 3) building and running production backend services. Deep in at least one backend language; Python preferred, Go, Kotlin/JVM or TypeScript/Node also welcome. Solid API and data-model design: REST/streaming APIs, PostgreSQL schema design, migrations, indexing, transactions. Distributed-systems fundamentals: async processing, queues or event streams, idempotency, retries, failure handling. Production experience on Kubernetes or a similar platform, with observability you actually used to debug an incident. Has shipped user-facing features on at least one client platform: Android, iOS, desktop or web (React/Next.js). Kotlin/Compose experience is a plus, not a gate. Willing to pick up the side of the stack they know less, and to learn agent and LLM systems on the job. Clear written communication: design docs, PR descriptions, RCAs. Nice to have Built on LLM APIs: tool calling, streaming, prompt caching, evals, or an agent loop of your own. MCP servers or clients, OAuth connector integrations, or sandboxed code execution. Kotlin Multiplatform / Compose Multiplatform, or native Android/iOS. Real-time systems: WebSockets/SSE, NATS, Kafka, or Temporal-style durable workflows. Go services, or performance and cost work with measurable before/after numbers. Open-source work or public writing we can read.

About Team & About Role:

 

As a Software Engineer (SE) in the Continuous Product Delivery (CPD) team, you will play a key role in providing long term stability and last mile delight to our customers. You will work closely with the core engineering team, product, and support org.

You will be working across Rubrik releases on our on-premise data backup & management offering, with a focus on the identity and access layer that secures it. You are expected to develop a strong understanding of our product and engineering architecture — particularly how authentication and authorization flow through the system, including our integrations with enterprise identity providers, directory services, and certificate-based trust chains.

We are seeking a highly skilled Golang developer with deep, practical experience in identity protocols (OIDC/OAuth 2.0, SAML 2.0) and applied cryptography/PKI. As a Software Engineer on this team, you will be responsible for designing, building, and hardening the systems that authenticate users, machines, and services across our platform — reasoning carefully about threat models, not just shipping features. You should have strong programming and troubleshooting skills, excellent design skills, and a solid understanding of distributed systems, OS fundamentals, and networking. The successful candidate will preferably have working knowledge of Active Directory and be able to work independently and as part of a team.

 

 
Responsibilities

  • Design, build, and harden identity and access flows — OIDC/OAuth 2.0, SAML 2.0, Active Directory integrations — that sit in front of mission-critical systems.
  • Own token and assertion lifecycle correctness: issuance, validation, expiry, rotation, and failure-mode handling for JWT/JWKS and SAML assertions.
  • Apply strong applied-cryptography and PKI practices (X.509 certs, key rotation, TLS) to keep the auth path secure by default, not as an afterthought.
  • Build and maintain reverse-proxy/HTTP-layer components (TLS termination, header handling) that front customer authentication traffic.
  • Debug and resolve customer-facing identity/access issues, working with support to triage escalations quickly.
  • Contribute to build/release and cross-platform packaging (Linux deb/rpm, Windows MSI) as needed.
  • Maintain a small Windows companion application written in C#/.NET.
  • Write and enhance end-to-end tests covering auth flows, failure modes, and edge cases (clock skew, revoked tokens, malformed assertions, etc.).
  • Document known issues, workarounds, and design decisions in the team knowledge base as the team and product mature.
  • Communicate clearly with product and engineering stakeholders on design tradeoffs, security posture, and escalation status.

Requirements

Must-have
  • Strong hands-on programming skills in Golang.
  • Deep, practical knowledge of identity protocols: OIDC/OAuth 2.0 and SAML 2.0 — including token/assertion internals, standard flows, and failure modes.
  • Working knowledge of Active Directory.
  • Applied cryptography/PKI experience: X.509, JWT/JWKS, key rotation, TLS.
  • Strong security engineering discipline — comfortable reasoning about threat models and building software to protect mission-critical systems, not just make features work.
  • Solid understanding of OS fundamentals, networking, and concurrency.
  • Working knowledge of Linux; comfortable writing shell/bash scripts.
  • Simple, effective written and verbal communication.
Nice-to-have
  • Directory internals (schema, bind operations).
  • HTTP internals and reverse proxying (TLS, header injection).
  • Build/release and cross-platform packaging (Linux deb/rpm, Windows MSI).
  • Secret-manager internals, Redis, Win32, policy engines.
  • Basic C#/.NET (to maintain the companion app).

Secure Every Identity, from AI to Human

Identity is the key to unlocking the potential of AI. Okta secures AI by building the trusted, neutral infrastructure that enables organizations to safely embrace this new era. This work requires a relentless drive to solve complex challenges with real-world stakes. We are looking for builders and owners who operate with speed and urgency and execute with excellence.

This is an opportunity to do career-defining work. We're all in on this mission. If you are too, let's talk.

About the Team & Impact
At Okta, Demo Engineering bridges the gap between product innovation and go-to-market execution—acting as a global force multiplier for our technical sales organization. We equip internal and partner Solution Engineers worldwide with the tools and environments needed to effortlessly demonstrate how Okta secures identities across workforces, customers, and AI agents.

In this role, your code directly powers Okta’s global sales engine. The demo architectures and interactive experiences you create will be leveraged by hundreds of field engineers across dozens of countries, influencing thousands of enterprise customer conversations. Operating within an engineering-first, collaborative culture focused on automation, modularity, and self-service, you will build the core platform that makes Okta’s field teams faster, sharper, and more scalable.

What You’ll Do

  • Architect Reusable Assets: Design and develop modular demo components and pre-configured product environments tailored to high-impact, solution-driven customer scenarios.
  • Capture Field Insights: Partner closely with global field teams to gather "Voice of the Customer" feedback—translating prospect expectations, preferences, and friction points into platform improvements.
  • Drive Platform Adoption: Team up with Field Readiness to champion the Demo Platform and accelerate usage across the broader go-to-market organization.
  • Measure & Optimize: Build telemetry, analytics, and reporting dashboards to monitor demo engagement and quantify field impact.
  • Launch New Capabilities: Collaborate cross-functionally with Product Management and Core Engineering to build demo-ready experiences ahead of new product releases.
  • Influence Product Roadmap: Represent field and customer insights during release planning to help shape future product direction.
  • Enable the Field: Author clear technical walkthroughs, demonstration guides, and video tutorials to empower self-service adoption.

What You Bring to the Table

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science/Engineering or equivalent practical experience.
  • Industry Experience: 5+ years of hands-on software development experience building Enterprise SaaS solutions.
  • Full-Stack & Cloud Expertise: Strong proficiency in React.js, Node.js, and AWS Serverless architectures (Lambda, DynamoDB, SQS, SNS).
  • Multi-Tenant Architecture: Proven background designing and implementing multi-tenant systems with strict tenant isolation.
  • DevOps & Automation: Practical experience with Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) or automated configuration management tools.
  • Identity & API Fluency: Solid experience integrating REST/GraphQL APIs with identity providers, backed by strong working knowledge of modern authentication and authorization standards (OAuth 2.0, OIDC, SAML).

How You Work

  • Globally Minded: Experienced in collaborating across time zones and supporting a distributed, international field organization.
  • Proactive Builder: Self-driven and resourceful—you spot gaps, propose solutions, and execute without needing micromanagement.
  • Cross-Functional Connector: Energized by working at the intersection of Sales, Product, and Engineering.
  • Systems Thinker: Capable of balancing fast-turnaround field requests with long-term architectural scalability and code reuse.
  • Customer-Obsessed: Skilled at distilling qualitative customer and field feedback into concrete technical requirements.

Bonus Points For

  • Prior experience on a Demo Engineering, Technical Marketing, or Developer Relations team.
  • Background in Presales, Solutions Engineering, or Customer-Facing Technical Consulting.
  • Hands-on familiarity with Okta or Auth0 platforms.

Join the team as our next Software engineer (L1) on Twilio’s Segment, Data platform

About the job

This position is needed to build new features and capabilities in the Twilio Segment Data platform.

As a Software Engineer on this team, you’ll build and scale systems that process several hundred thousands of data points per second. Helping our customers unlock value of their data from external systems and activate it to various destinations via Segment capabilities. You will work on high-scale ingestion and data processing systems. 

We iterate quickly on these products and features and learn new things daily — all while writing quality code. We work closely with product and design and solve some of the toughest engineering problems to unlock new possibilities for our customers. If you get excited by building products with high customer impact — this is the place for you.

Responsibilities

In this role, you’ll:

  • Design and deliver robust, high-scale routing experiences for Data Pipelines for Twilio Segment.
  • Operate always-available, complex distributed systems in cloud environments.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with design, product, and other engineers to define solutions that balance usability, performance, and long-term architecture.
  • Communicate technical decisions clearly - articulating trade-offs, customer impact, and team alignment.
  • Participate in an on-call rotation for our managed services. Troubleshoot and improve system reliability, debugging issues and refining operational tooling and processes.

Qualifications 

Twilio values diverse experiences from all kinds of industries, and we encourage everyone who meets the required qualifications to apply. If your career is just starting or hasn't followed a traditional path, don't let that stop you from considering Twilio. We are always looking for people who will bring something new to the table!

*Required:

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or related field.
  • Hands-on experience with high-scale messaging/streaming systems and processing engines (several thousand events/sec). 
  • 1-2 years experience writing production-grade code in a modern programming language.
  • Proficient programming experience in Go, Java, Python or similar object-oriented languages.
  • Experience operating large-scale, distributed systems on top of cloud infrastructure.

Read the diff, test the result and be able to explain what you're shipping. 'The model wrote it' isn't a debugging strategy. Ask good questions when the brief is fuzzy. Explain trade-offs, suggest a practical way forward and use evidence before declaring that something needs fixing. How do we work?
Whatever your role, our values describe what we ask of each other.

Be a bridger
Look beyond your own role. Ask questions, share context and help others get unstuck. That may mean bringing the right people together or picking up a problem that doesn’t necessarily fit neatly into your job description.

Care loudly
We want your perspective, not just your agreement. Speak up when something isn’t working or someone needs support. Give honest feedback with respect for the person receiving it. Don’t let an uncomfortable conversation become an unspoken problem.

Own the outcome
Take responsibility for the result, not just your part in the process. Use AI to move the work forward, not to outsource your judgment. Make the call, check whether it worked and change course when it didn’t. If something goes wrong, own it and help fix it.
